text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's Moslem chairman of the collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic during his visit to Saudi Arabia, says that Croat and Serb forces are still working on dissolution of Bosnia, Bosnian news agency BH PRESS reports.
- Bosnia's trade union appeal to Moslem-Croat federal authorities not to block the work of the federal House of Representatives scheduled for March 18 and to try to solve accumulated social problems.

- A World Bank official from Washington says during his visit to Sarajevo that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme in Bosnia is going slow and that it's necessary to provide immediately new funds for reconstruction programme.
- 232 Croat refugee families returned to Bugojno as it was planned by UNHCR pilot-project of refugee returns.
- More than 50 percent of interviewees in a poll think that only a new peace conference can save the peace process.

- Bosnia has chances to join NATO-led programme "Partnership for peace", Muhamed Sacirbey, Bosnian ambassador to the United Nations says. Bosnia's senior military officials think that once Bosnia joins that programme, its military potential will be reinforced.

- The federation's House of Representatives will meet on Tuesday. Discussion will be focused on appointment of a new president of the Moslem-Croat federation and his deputy. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
